- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- When sentiment turns negative (≤-1.0) mid-period, model often overshoots downward; cap downward corrections at 3–5% below recent low.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model frequently overcorrects; apply a “lagged mean reversion” rule: subtract 1–2% of the spike magnitude from next forecast.
- If sentiment flips from positive to negative within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; force a 1–3% downward bias in forecast horizon.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is bullish; apply a 1–3% downward adjustment to first 5 days.
- When sentiment is mixed (±0.5–1.0), model often averages out; use sentiment-weighted smoothing: higher weight to recent sentiment if >0.5, lower if <0.5.
